papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing highlights innovative optimization strategies tailored for both cloud and edge environments, addressing challenges like user mobility and workload variability. Key contributions include the development of adaptive algorithms that improve resource allocation efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving video streaming and mmWave networks. However, gaps remain in evaluating the scalability and real-world applicability of these approaches, emphasizing the need for further research into hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms.
literature_tension_graph: Existing literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation presents conflicting assumptions regarding the adaptability of algorithms to dynamic environments. While P2 claims that its MADRL-AHHO algorithm improves allocation accuracy under dynamic workloads, it does not fully explore performance under extreme conditions, leaving a gap in evaluation. Conversely, P4 emphasizes the necessity for adaptive solutions in highly dynamic environments but focuses primarily on mobility, neglecting static resource allocation strategies. This presents a mechanism conflict where existing approaches fail to reconcile the need for both dynamic adaptability and static efficiency in resource allocation. The unresolved condition is the lack of comprehensive evaluation of hybrid optimization techniques that can address both aspects. This tension suggests a research direction focused on developing a robust MARL framework that integrates both dynamic adaptability and static resource management strategies, potentially enhancing overall resource allocation efficiency in cloud environments.
scholarly_positioning: Prior research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing has predominantly focused on optimizing strategies for static workloads and user mobility, yet these approaches often fail to adapt dynamically to fluctuating demands and resource constraints. Existing methodologies, while innovative, do not comprehensively address the scalability and real-world applicability of their proposed solutions, particularly under extreme dynamic conditions. This research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a robust MARL framework that integrates hybrid optimization techniques and adaptive incentive mechanisms, thereby enhancing resource allocation efficiency in cloud environments. By situating this work within the ongoing discourse on dynamic resource management, it seeks to contribute a novel perspective that emphasizes the need for adaptive solutions capable of addressing the complexities of modern cloud computing landscapes.
research_scope: This study will focus on the optimization of dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting video streaming applications that require adaptive resource management due to fluctuating user demands. The proposed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework will integrate hybrid optimization techniques and adaptive incentive mechanisms to enhance resource allocation efficiency over a six-month evaluation period. A control group will consist of traditional static resource allocation strategies for comparison. Primary outcomes will include the improvement in resource utilization rates and system throughput, while secondary outcomes will assess user satisfaction and latency metrics. This research aims to provide empirical evidence on the effectiveness of adaptive MARL strategies in real-world cloud computing scenarios.

technical_feasibility: The proposed study requires access to open-source MARL models for implementation and testing, as well as GPU resources for training the models efficiently. Additionally, it may require labeled datasets for evaluating resource allocation performance metrics. Since user satisfaction and trust are key outcomes, a human-subject design will be necessary to gather qualitative feedback, which also requires ethics approval. To enhance interpretability, methods for analyzing internal representations may be beneficial, necessitating access to models that allow for hidden-state extraction. A feasible adjustment would be to focus on using existing open-source MARL frameworks and datasets, while ensuring ethical guidelines are followed for user studies.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in optimizing resource allocation for dynamic workloads in cloud computing environments; however, the literature tension graph shows unresolved tension regarding the adaptability of existing algorithms to both dynamic and static resource allocation strategies, leaving unclear whether hybrid optimization techniques can enhance performance under extreme conditions. This matters practically because efficient resource allocation is crucial for maintaining service quality in fluctuating user demands; therefore, this study investigates the integration of hybrid optimization techniques within a MARL framework to improve resource allocation efficiency in cloud environments focused on video streaming applications.
question: How does the integration of hybrid optimization techniques within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework improve resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in dynamic cloud computing environments for video streaming applications compared to traditional static resource allocation strategies?

The problem is empirically testable through the proposed framework and evaluation metrics, making it relevant for committee interest. However, the strongest reason for potential rejection could be the perceived overlap with existing research without clear differentiation. To enhance the depth and research-worthiness, the problem could be reframed to focus specifically on quantifying the impact of hybrid optimization techniques on user satisfaction and system throughput in real-world scenarios, rather than broadly addressing resource allocation efficiency.

theoretical_mechanism: In this research, the independent variable is the integration of hybrid optimization techniques within the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework. The mediator is the adaptive resource allocation strategy that emerges from the interaction of multiple agents, which optimizes resource distribution based on real-time demand. The moderator is the dynamic nature of user workloads, influencing the effectiveness of the optimization techniques. The dependent variables are system-level outcomes, such as resource utilization rates and system throughput, and user-level outcomes, including user satisfaction and latency metrics. The theoretical framework is grounded in reinforcement learning principles, where agents learn to adapt their strategies based on feedback from the environment. The causal chain suggests that effective resource allocation (mediated by adaptive strategies) leads to improved system performance and user satisfaction. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of hybrid optimization techniques in real-world scenarios and the impact of adaptive strategies on user perceptions of service quality.
hypothesis: The integration of hybrid optimization techniques within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will lead to higher resource utilization rates compared to traditional static resource allocation strategies, mediated by improved adaptive resource allocation strategies, resulting in increased user satisfaction in dynamic cloud computing environments for video streaming applications.

proposal: This research investigates the integration of hybrid optimization techniques within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to enhance dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing, specifically targeting video streaming applications that experience fluctuating user demands. The novelty of this study lies in its focus on combining genetic algorithms with MARL to create a robust adaptive resource allocation strategy that addresses the limitations of existing static approaches, which often fail to adapt to real-time workload variations as highlighted in the literature. The identified gap emphasizes the need for a unified approach that reconciles the adaptability of algorithms to both dynamic and static conditions, a tension not sufficiently resolved in prior work, particularly in the context of user mobility and link dynamics in cloud environments. The research question is: How does the integration of hybrid optimization techniques within a MARL framework improve resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in dynamic cloud computing environments for video streaming applications compared to traditional static resource allocation strategies? The theoretical mechanism posits that hybrid optimization techniques (independent variable) will enhance adaptive resource allocation strategies (mediator), leading to improved resource utilization rates and user satisfaction (dependent variables), moderated by the dynamic nature of user workloads. The falsifiable hypothesis states that the integration of hybrid optimization techniques will yield higher resource utilization rates compared to traditional static strategies, mediated by enhanced adaptive resource allocation, resulting in increased user satisfaction. Constructs will be operationalized through metrics such as resource utilization rates (measured via cloud resource management tools), user satisfaction (assessed through surveys), and system throughput (analyzed through performance logs). The methodology will involve a comparative study using a control group of traditional static allocation strategies, with specific statistical analyses, such as ANOVA, to validate the findings and controls for confounding variables like user demand variability. This research aims to provide theoretical advancements in adaptive resource allocation strategies, technical innovations in hybrid optimization mechanisms, and empirical evidence demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework, while acknowledging limitations such as potential confounding factors affecting cloud performance and the need for ethical considerations in user studies.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: understandable but partially broad or insufficiently operationalized
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal identifies a relevant research problem in dynamic resource allocation using MARL but lacks precise operational definitions for key constructs such as 'hybrid optimization techniques' and 'adaptive resource allocation strategies'. The framing is somewhat broad and could benefit from clearer boundaries. Major weaknesses: Key concepts are not sufficiently operationalized, and the research question is somewhat vague, lacking specificity in the context of existing literature. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal must provide clearer definitions of key constructs and a more focused research question that delineates the boundaries of the study.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: generally connected but some weak transitions or unsupported assumptions
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from the problem to the hypothesis, but some assumptions regarding the effectiveness of hybrid techniques are not sufficiently justified. The causal claims need stronger empirical backing. Major weaknesses: Weak transitions between the theoretical mechanism and the proposed methodology, leading to some unsupported assumptions about the effectiveness of the hybrid approach. Next band requirements: Strengthening the justification for causal claims and ensuring that all components of the proposal are tightly connected would improve coherence.

While the proposal claims novelty through the integration of hybrid optimization techniques, it does not sufficiently differentiate itself from existing MARL frameworks. The contribution appears to be a combination of existing ideas rather than a genuinely new framework. Major weaknesses: The novelty claim lacks specificity and depth, making it difficult to assess its true contribution to the field. Next band requirements: To enhance the novelty score, the proposal should clearly articulate how the integration of hybrid techniques distinctly advances the field and provide concrete examples.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for comparative studies; however, it lacks detailed descriptions of how confounding variables will be controlled and how metrics will be validated. Major weaknesses: Insufficient detail on the experimental design and controls, particularly regarding how to handle confounding variables and ensure reproducibility. Next band requirements: Incorporating more robust controls and detailed descriptions of the evaluation metrics and statistical analyses would enhance the methodological rigor.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: relevant literature used but somewhat surface-level
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature but does not critically synthesize it or clearly identify gaps in a way that positions the research within ongoing debates. Major weaknesses: Lacks depth in literature review and fails to adequately position the research against existing work, missing opportunities to highlight unresolved tensions. Next band requirements: A more critical synthesis of the literature and a clearer articulation of how the proposed research addresses identified gaps would strengthen scholarly positioning.

rubric_scores.level: 5-6: strong master-level but limited theoretical depth
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates some theoretical grounding but lacks depth in discussing the mechanisms and implications of the proposed research. Major weaknesses: Limited discussion of theoretical mechanisms and implications, which detracts from the overall academic depth. Next band requirements: A more thorough exploration of the theoretical implications and a discussion of potential limitations and failure cases would enhance academic depth.

The writing is generally clear and organized, but some areas lack precision and conciseness, which affects readability. Major weaknesses: Some sections are verbose and could be more concise, leading to minor issues with clarity. Next band requirements: Improving conciseness and ensuring precision in terminology would enhance the overall presentation quality.

Major weaknesses: Lacks clear operational definitions for key constructs.; Novelty claims are not sufficiently differentiated from existing research.; Methodological details are incomplete, particularly regarding controls. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Provide clearer definitions and operationalizations of key constructs.; Articulate a more distinct theoretical contribution and novelty.; Enhance methodological rigor with detailed controls and validation strategies. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the depth and rigor expected at the PhD level, requiring significant improvements to achieve genuine research maturity.
